name: Apify
description: Apify is the scraping-and-automation platform a lot of AI data pipelines quietly sit on. You run ready-made Actors to pull web pages, social feeds, search results and maps data, or you write your own Actor and sell it in the Apify Store. The money angle is the real draw: publish an Actor, set a price per event, and keep roughly 80% of every sale while Apify handles billing, hosting and proxies. It is built for people who are fine with APIs, JSON and a bit of JavaScript, not for someone who wants a click-and-go dashboard.
pricing_details: Apify runs on a subscription plus pay-as-you-go model, and every paid plan's fee comes back as prepaid usage you spend on platform compute or on Store Actors. Free is $0 with $5 of monthly credit and compute at $0.20 per compute unit (1 CU is 1 GB of RAM for one hour). Starter is $19/month, gives $19 of prepaid usage, keeps compute at $0.20/CU and adds a small Bronze discount on Store Actors. Scale is $199/month with $199 prepaid, cheaper compute at $0.16/CU and a Silver Store discount. Business is $999/month with $999 prepaid, $0.13/CU and a Gold discount. Add-ons stack on top: extra concurrent runs cost $5 per run, Actor RAM is $1 per GB, datacenter proxies start at $0.60 per IP, residential proxies run about $8 per GB, Google SERP proxies are $2.50 per 1,000 results on the lower plans, and the unblocker is $1.50 per 1,000 requests. There is also a Creator plan that hands developers $500 of free usage over six months to build and test Actors and AI agents. On the earning side, the flagship model is pay-per-event (PPE): you define an event - a profile scraped, a search page returned - and buyers pay per event, which also gets your Actor priority placement in the Store. Pay-per-result still exists but Apify now treats it as a kind of event inside PPE. The developer keeps roughly 80% of compliant Actor revenue and Apify takes the rest as platform commission; refunds and chargebacks come out of your net. Payouts clear monthly - invoices go out on the 11th, there is a review window through the 14th, and funds are released around the 21st-25th - with a $100 minimum for bank transfer and $20 for PayPal. Note the old rental model is being retired: no new rental listings after April 1, 2026, and full retirement on October 1, 2026, so do not build anything new on it.
pros: The Store is a genuine distribution channel, not just a gallery. You list an Actor, set pay-per-event pricing, and Apify takes care of billing, hosting, proxies and payouts - the developer share lands around 80%, which is a rare setup where a solo builder can earn passive income from a scraper they wrote once

The free tier is usable for real work: $5 of monthly credit, no credit card, and a catalog of thousands of pre-built Actors (Instagram, Google Maps, LinkedIn, website crawlers) you can point at a URL and get clean JSON in minutes without writing code

It scales past hobby level when you need it - 256 GB Actor RAM, hundreds of concurrent runs and built-in proxy pools on the top plan mean the same platform that runs a $5 test handles an enterprise crawl, and the Creator plan's $500 free usage covers the build-and-test phase

Strong AI fit: Actors are commonly used to feed RAG pipelines, agents and enrichment workflows, and the PPE model is designed to be called by AI/MCP tooling, so it slots into the automation stacks people are already selling
cons: It is a developer platform and it acts like one. The console is dense, pricing is three layers deep (subscription, compute units, per-Actor fees), and building your own Actor means writing JavaScript and reading API docs - there is no friendly 'describe it and go' flow for a non-technical operator

Costs creep in ways the headline plan price hides. Compute units, proxy traffic, storage reads and writes, and per-run add-ons all bill separately, and a runaway crawl can burn through prepaid credit before you notice. You need to watch the usage dashboard, not just the plan fee

Earning from the Store is not automatic money. You are competing against thousands of existing Actors, most niches already have a popular option, and payout is monthly with a $100 bank minimum - plus the rental model is dead as of October 2026, so the old set-and-forget route is gone and you have to price per event to get placement

faq.question: How much does Apify actually cost in 2026?
faq.answer: The plans are Free ($0, $5 monthly credit), Starter ($19/month), Scale ($199/month) and Business ($999/month), and on every paid tier the subscription fee comes back to you as prepaid usage you spend on compute or Store Actors. Compute runs $0.20 per compute unit on Free and Starter, $0.16 on Scale and $0.13 on Business (1 CU is 1 GB of RAM for an hour). Real bills are bigger than the plan price because proxies, storage and add-ons bill separately - residential proxies are about $8 per GB, extra concurrent runs $5 each, and Actor RAM $1 per GB. For a small project the Free or $19 plan is often enough; heavy crawling is where the pay-as-you-go usage becomes the real cost.

faq.question: Can you actually make money with Apify?
faq.answer: Yes, and there are two honest paths. The first is publishing Actors: you build a scraper, list it in the Apify Store with pay-per-event pricing, and earn roughly 80% of every sale while Apify handles billing, hosting and payouts - a good niche Actor can earn while you sleep, but you are competing with thousands of existing listings. The second is selling the output rather than the tool: run Actors to deliver lead lists, competitor price monitoring, market data or enrichment feeds as a service to clients, and bill a monthly retainer. The service route pays faster and more reliably than the Store route; the Store route is the one that can become passive.

faq.question: Do I need to know how to code to use Apify?
faq.answer: Not to use it, but yes to build with it. Running existing Store Actors is click-and-configure - pick one, feed it a URL or a keyword list, and get JSON back - so a non-coder can complete real scraping jobs. Writing your own Actor, wiring webhooks, or feeding an AI agent assumes you are comfortable with JavaScript, REST APIs and JSON. If you only want ready-made scrapers, treat Apify as a paid utility; if you want to earn from it, budget for learning the SDK.

content:
# Apify Review 2026: The Scraper Store You Can Actually Earn From

I have run Apify for client work since late 2025 - lead lists for a B2B agency, price monitoring for a small e-commerce seller, and a competitor-tracking feed for a marketing team. The platform is not glamorous and it will not win a design award, but it does one thing better than almost anyone: it turns a scraper you wrote once into something you can sell repeatedly.

## What Apify Actually Is

Apify is a cloud platform for web scraping and browser automation. The unit of work is an Actor - a packaged script that takes an input, runs in the cloud, and returns a dataset. Thousands of Actors already exist in the Apify Store: Instagram and TikTok profile scrapers, Google Maps and search scrapers, LinkedIn tools, e-commerce price trackers, generic website crawlers. You pick one, feed it a URL or a keyword list, and get clean JSON back in minutes. If nothing fits, you write your own Actor in JavaScript using the Apify SDK and publish it.

The infrastructure underneath is the part you stop noticing: proxy pools, retries, anti-bot handling, scheduling, storage and a REST API. You do not have to stand up your own server farm or babysit a rotating proxy list. That is the value - not the scrapers themselves, which anyone can write, but the billing, hosting and distribution wrapped around them.

## The Money Angle

This is why Apify is on an AI-tools site rather than buried in a developer blog. There are two ways to earn, and they behave very differently.

**1. Publish an Actor and get paid per event.** The Apify Store is a marketplace with real buyers. You list your Actor, choose pay-per-event pricing (a profile scraped, a page returned, an export generated), and Apify handles the transaction - it takes the payment, hosts the run, and pays you out monthly. The developer keeps roughly 80% of compliant revenue. Write a scraper that solves a specific, boring problem - a niche directory, a regional marketplace, an obscure API - and it can earn for years while you do nothing. The catch is competition: popular niches are already crowded, and a new listing gets no traffic until it earns reviews and placement.

**2. Sell the data, not the tool.** This is the faster, more reliable path. Clients rarely want to learn a scraping console; they want a spreadsheet of leads, a weekly price report, or a competitor feed. You run the Actors in the background, clean the output, and deliver the result on a retainer. A B2B lead-gen package at $1,000-3,000 a month is common, and the Apify usage behind it is usually a small fraction of that. It is a service business, so you own the client relationship and the delivery - but it pays now, not eventually.

The two combine well: build a delivery service for a niche, and once the scraper is stable, list a version in the Store as a side earner.

## What It Really Costs

The plans are Free ($0, $5 of monthly credit), Starter ($19/month), Scale ($199/month) and Business ($999/month). On every paid tier, the subscription fee returns as prepaid usage you spend on compute or on Store Actors - so $19 buys $19 of platform usage, not just access.

Compute is billed per compute unit: $0.20/CU on Free and Starter, $0.16 on Scale, $0.13 on Business. One CU is 1 GB of RAM for an hour, so a light Actor scraping a few hundred pages a day sits well inside the free or $19 tier. The bill grows with proxies and volume: residential proxies run about $8 per GB, datacenter IPs from $0.60 each, extra concurrent runs $5 each, and Actor RAM $1 per GB. Storage reads and writes bill separately too.

The number that surprises people is not the plan fee - it is a runaway crawl that burns prepaid credit overnight. Watch the usage dashboard for the first month.

If you are building rather than buying, the Creator plan gives you $500 of free usage over six months to develop and test Actors. That covers the expensive part of learning the SDK.

## Where It Falls Apart

It is a developer tool wearing a product's clothes. The console is dense, the pricing has three layers, and building an Actor means JavaScript and API docs. A non-technical operator can run existing Actors all day, but the moment something needs customising, you are reading code.

Costs are easy to lose track of. Subscription, compute units, proxies, storage and per-run add-ons all bill on separate lines, and it is genuinely hard to predict a monthly bill from the pricing page alone.

And earning from the Store is not passive income out of the box. Most niches have a dominant Actor already, payouts are monthly with a $100 minimum for bank transfer, and the old rental model - the set-and-forget route - is being retired: no new rental listings after April 1, 2026, and full shutdown on October 1, 2026. If you want Store income now, you price per event and you earn it.

## Who Should Pay

Use Apify if you need web data at any scale and do not want to run your own scraping infrastructure, or if you have an idea for a scraper that a specific audience would pay for and you want a marketplace to sell it through. The free tier is enough to prove both ideas before you spend anything.

Skip it if you want a no-code automation builder - Make, n8n and Zapier are friendlier for connecting apps without writing code. And if you just need one-off data, a freelance scraper on Upwork will be cheaper than learning the platform. Apify pays off when you either scrape repeatedly or sell what you scrape, not when you do it once.
